body_html:
Learning how to use gustar is a rite of passage for every Spanish learner. The problem is that gustar doesn’t mean “to like” in the way English works. It means something closer to “to be pleasing to”. So in Me gusta el café, the coffee is the subject: coffee is pleasing to me. Once you see that the sentence works “backwards”, every gustar mistake becomes easy to fix.

Key takeaways
  • The thing you like is the subject: me gusta el libro, me gustan los libros.
  • The person who likes is an indirect object pronoun: me, te, le, nos, os, les.
  • Add a mí, a ti, a Juan for emphasis or clarity: A Juan le gusta el fútbol.
  • Me gustas is romantic; for friends say Me caes bien.
{{toc}}

How to use gustar: the structure

Who likesPronounOne thing / an actionSeveral things
Imeme gusta el téme gustan los gatos
you (tú)tete gusta bailarte gustan las flores
he / she / you (usted)lele gusta leerle gustan las novelas
wenosnos gusta la playanos gustan las montañas
you all (Spain)osos gusta el planos gustan los planes
they / you alllesles gusta viajarles gustan los museos

The verb agrees with the thing liked, not the person. That’s why it’s almost always gusta or gustan. The RAE dictionary defines this use of gustar as something being pleasing or attractive to someone.

Gusta or gustan?

  • Singular noun: Me gusta la música.
  • Plural noun: Me gustan las películas de terror.
  • Verb (infinitive), even several: Me gusta cocinar y bailar. (singular)

A mí me gusta: emphasis and clarity

Spanish often adds a + person before the pronoun:

  • Emphasis: A mí me gusta el verano, pero a ella no. I like summer, but she doesn’t.
  • Clarity: le can mean him, her or you, so A Ana le gusta el jazz makes it clear.
  • Short answers: —Me encanta este sitio. —A mí también. / —No me gusta el café. —A mí tampoco.

The pronoun stays even with a mí: A mí me gusta, never A mí gusta. I explain more about this front-loading in {{link:spanish-word-order|Spanish word order}}.

{{image:2}}

Me gustas vs me caes bien

This is where gustar mistakes become awkward. Saying Me gustas to a person means “I like you” in a romantic or physical way. To say you like someone as a person or friend, use Me caes bien (literally, you fall well to me):

  • Tu hermano me cae muy bien. I really like your brother (he’s nice).
  • Me gustas mucho. I really like you (I’m attracted to you).

For flirting and dating phrases, see {{link:how-to-flirt-in-spanish|how to flirt in Spanish}}, and for the next step, {{link:te-quiero-vs-te-amo|te quiero vs te amo}}.

{{book:love-slowly}}

Verbs that work like gustar

VerbMeaningExample
encantarto love (things)Me encanta el chocolate.
interesarto interestNos interesa la historia.
molestarto botherMe molesta el ruido.
dolerto hurtMe duelen los pies.
faltarto be missing, lackTe falta sal.
importarto matterNo me importa.
antojarseto feel like, crave (Latin America)¿Se te antoja un café?
apetecerto feel like (Spain)¿Te apetece un café?
quedarto have left, to fitMe quedan cien pesos.

More on that last one in {{link:quedar-vs-quedarse|quedar vs quedarse}}.

Intensity: mucho, encantar and no

  • Me gusta mucho. I like it a lot. (Not me gusta muy.)
  • Me encanta. I love it. (Already strong: avoid me encanta mucho.)
  • No me gusta nada. I don’t like it at all.
  • No me gusta mucho. I don’t really like it.

Real conversations

  • A: ¿Te gusta la comida mexicana? (Do you like Mexican food?)
  • B: Me encanta. Me gustan mucho los tacos, pero no me gusta el picante. (I love it. I really like tacos, but I don’t like spicy food.)
  • A: ¡A mí tampoco! A mi novio sí le gusta, pero yo no lo aguanto. (Me neither! My boyfriend likes it, but I can’t stand it.)

Common gustar mistakes

IncorrectCorrectWhy
Yo gusto el café.Me gusta el café.The coffee is the subject
Me gusta los perros.Me gustan los perros.Plural subject: gustan
A mí gusta bailar.A mí me gusta bailar.Keep the pronoun
Ella le gusta el cine.A ella le gusta el cine.Needs a
Me gustas (to a new friend)Me caes bien.Avoid a romantic message
Me gusta muy.Me gusta mucho.After a verb: mucho
{{image:3}}

Try it yourself

  1. We like this restaurant. (Nos gusta este restaurante.)
  2. My parents love to travel. (A mis padres les encanta viajar.)
  3. My head hurts. (Me duele la cabeza.)
  4. Do you like horror movies? (¿Te gustan las películas de terror?)
  5. I like your sister, she’s very nice. (Tu hermana me cae muy bien.)

Gustar is one of the mistake families in {{link:common-spanish-mistakes|my guide to common Spanish mistakes}}.

{{quiz}}

Final thoughts

Think “is pleasing to” and gustar falls into place: the thing liked is the subject, the person is the pronoun, and the verb agrees with the thing. Add a mí for emphasis, use me caes bien for friends, and save me gustas for someone special.

faq.q: How do you use gustar in Spanish?
faq.a: Gustar works like “to be pleasing to”. The thing liked is the subject, and the person who likes is an indirect object pronoun: Me gusta el café, Me gustan los perros.

faq.q: What is the difference between me gusta and me gustan?
faq.a: Me gusta is used with one thing or with verbs (me gusta leer). Me gustan is used with plural things (me gustan los libros).

faq.q: Does me gustas mean I like you?
faq.a: Yes, but romantically or physically. To say you like someone as a friend, say Me caes bien.
